elements.evidence: Section 9.6 expressly permits Customer to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.6 specifies thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section 9.6 expressly requires written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 9.6 requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination, which provides the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants the convenience-termination right solely to Customer. Vendor's other termination rights are limited to specified cause-based events, and no Vendor convenience right is granted.
Section 9.6 expressly grants Customer a convenience-termination right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires a notice period of 60–90 days.
elements.evidence: Section 9.6 requires only thirty (30) days' prior notice, not a notice period within the 60–90-day fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 9.6 prohibits any early-termination charge or penalty, so the applicable fee is zero and therefore does not exceed three months' fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted, so there is no Vendor convenience right that could be exercised before the end of a term.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days' notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience right is granted; accordingly, the condition triggering this notice requirement is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline fully satisfies the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day written convenience right, a refund of prepaid post-termination fees, and Vendor receives no corresponding convenience right. The fallback is independently unsatisfied because the Customer notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days. The amendment preserves the existing cause-based termination regime and introduces no contradiction. It is not strictly minimal because it additionally grants termination 'in whole or in part' and expressly prohibits all early-termination charges, language broader than necessary to state the enumerated preferred requirements. The drafting is otherwise clear and operative.
